issue: The rules are labelled "light rules = 80 GB rank boundaries", but they are drawn as horizontal lines across the plot. A rank boundary is a division between GPUs (8 GPUs side by side), which can only be represented by vertical partitions; horizontal lines at 80 GB intervals are capacity gridlines, not rank boundaries. The caption repeats the mislabel ("the 80 GB rank-boundary lines are a visualization guide").
evidence: Rendered page 146: subtitle "(light rules = 80 GB rank boundaries)" above a set of horizontal light rules; caption: "…the 80 GB rank-boundary lines are a visualization guide; sharding, KV partitioning, interconnect must be validated per rank." No vertical partition of the 640 GB pool into 8 × 80 GB is drawn anywhere.
acceptance_test: Rename the rules to "80 GB capacity gridlines" in both the figure subtitle and the caption, or draw eight vertical partitions labelled R0…R7 to show the actual rank boundaries. Confirm the caption's caveat about per-rank validation still reads correctly against whichever treatment is chosen.

issue: The concurrency consequence is stated only for two of the three bars, and the 128K figure is loose: "only ~1–2 at 128K". 436 / 335 = 1.30, i.e. one concurrent request (floor), not "~1–2". The 32K case (436 / 84 = 5.19 → 5 concurrent) is omitted entirely, even though the figure draws that bar.
evidence: Rendered page 146 caption: "…consuming the fixed ~436 GB KV budget (17.5 concurrent at 9.5K, floor 17; only ~1–2 at 128K)". Figure labels: KV 24.9 GB (9.5K), KV 84 GB (32K), KV 335 GB (128K). 436/24.9 = 17.5 ✓; 436/84 = 5.19; 436/335 = 1.30.
acceptance_test: State all three: "17.5 → 17 concurrent at 9.5K; 5.2 → 5 at 32K; 1.3 → 1 at 128K", using the same floor discipline already applied at 9.5K. Consider printing the concurrency figure under each bar in the figure itself so the reader can read capacity directly off the chart.

acceptance_test: Revise the figure to separate execution resources from storage tiers, or explicitly mark tensor cores as compute-only and outside the capacity gradient; verify a reader does not infer tensor cores have memory capacity.

issue: The ladder is presented as a "speed↔capacity↔distance" ranking, but the ordering of HBM above GPU interconnect is a latency/distance statement, not a bandwidth statement: HBM bandwidth (3.35 TB/s on H100) is roughly 7× NVLink bandwidth (~450 GB/s). evidence: Rendered page 152 caption: "The gradient of speed↔capacity↔distance is why compute, memory bandwidth, memory capacity and interconnect bandwidth are distinct architectural constraints…" The figure places "GPU interconnect" below "HBM (GPU memory)" on a single monotone ladder.

issue: The caption states "the peak roofline is 989 TFLOPS (H100) / 1,979 TFLOPS (H200)". This is wrong and it contradicts the figure it captions: the drawing shows both curves plateauing at a single annotated "compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS", and the figure's own ridge labels (295 for H100, 206 for H200) are only consistent with a 989 TFLOPS peak for both devices. H200 is the same compute die as H100: FP16 dense = 989 TFLOPS (1,979 TFLOPS is the *sparsity* figure, and 1,979 is also H100/H200 FP8 dense). A reader who adopts the caption's 1,979 for H200 will compute an H200 ridge of 1,979/4.8 = 412 FLOP/byte instead of 206, and will misplace the compute-bound boundary.
evidence: Rendered page 159 caption: "Convention: a multiply-add counts as 2 FLOPs, so the peak roofline is 989 TFLOPS (H100) / 1,979 TFLOPS (H200)." Figure: one shared plateau annotated "compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS"; ridge labels "ridge = 295" (H100) and "ridge = 206" (H200). Check: 989/3.35 = 295 ✓ and 989/4.8 = 206 ✓; 1,979/4.8 = 412 ✗ (matches no label in the figure).
acceptance_test: Correct the caption to "the peak roofline is 989 TFLOPS dense FP16 for both H100 and H200 (1,979 TFLOPS is the sparsity figure, and the FP8 dense figure)", and confirm the figure's plateau annotation and both ridge labels remain consistent with 989 TFLOPS. Add a regression check that no H200 dense-FP16 peak of 1,979 appears anywhere in the book.

issue: The caption contains a direct self-contradiction about the same operating point: "decode (batch=1) sits to the left, on the compute-bound side; decode (batch=1) sits to the left, on the memory-bound slope". Decode at batch=1 cannot be on both sides. The correct statement (per the facing page) is that decode at batch=1 sits at ≈1 FLOP/byte, far left, on the memory-bound slope, and that batching moves it rightward up that slope. Two further clauses are garbled: "the ridge point is the memory-bound slope (per-GPU)" (the ridge is where the memory-bound slope meets the compute-bound plateau) and "host-level attainable performance adds additional depends on scheduling and communication".
evidence: Rendered page 159 caption, sentences 3–5: "…Prefill (9.2K input) sits to the right of the compute-bound ridge (batch=1) — it is not a measured latency; decode (batch=1) sits to the left, on the compute-bound side; decode (batch=1) sits to the left, on the memory-bound slope and continues batching climbs the slope as batch grows." Facing page (printed 140): "decode intensity ≈ 1 FLOP/byte at batch=1 and ≈ 32 FLOP/byte at batch=32".
acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption so each operating point is described exactly once and consistently: prefill (9.2K) right of the ridge; decode batch=1 left of the ridge on the memory-bound slope; decode batched climbing that slope toward the ridge. Replace "the ridge point is the memory-bound slope" with "the ridge point is where the memory-bound slope meets the compute-bound plateau", and fix "adds additional depends on" to "additionally depends on". Confirm no clause remains that places decode batch=1 on the compute-bound side.

issue: The three vertical guides must span 1.65 decades on the log x-axis: H200 ridge 206 (just above 10²), H100 ridge 295 (mid-way between 10² and 10³), prefill 9.2K (immediately left of 10⁴). In the rendered page the orange prefill guide and the blue ridge guide appear separated by only a small fraction of a decade, and the orange guide appears to sit to the LEFT of the blue one — which would place the prefill operating point left of the ridge, the exact opposite of the caption's claim ("Prefill (9.2K input) sits to the right of the compute-bound ridge"). The separation between the decode ridge and the prefill operating point is the single most important thing this figure exists to show, so it cannot be left to a fraction of a decade.
evidence: Rendered page 159: x-axis ticks 10⁻¹…10⁴; the orange dotted guide descends from the "prefill 9.2K intensity = 9.2K FLOP/byte" label and the blue dotted guide is drawn close beside it, both in the region between the 10³ and 10⁴ ticks rather than at 10²·³, 10²·⁵ and 10³·⁹⁶. Expected x-positions (55 px/decade, 10⁻¹ at x≈127): 206 → x≈307; 295 → x≈316; 9,200 → x≈396.
acceptance_test: Measure the three guide lines in the vector source and confirm they land at 206, 295 and 9,200 FLOP/byte on the log axis (i.e. 10²·³¹, 10²·⁴⁷, 10³·⁹⁶), with the orange prefill guide to the RIGHT of both ridge guides. If the guides are drawn at the wrong positions, reposition them and re-check that the caption's "prefill sits to the right of the ridge" is visually true. Escalate to P1 if the orange guide is confirmed left of the ridge guides.

issue: The caption's frame-count identity is written incorrectly: "For aligned F = 4k+1, F = 1+4(T_j−1) = 31 latent time positions correspond to 121 frames." As written, 1 + 4(T_j−1) with T_j = 31 equals 121, not 31, and the symbol F (frames) is used for the latent-time-position count. The figure's own box states the correct identity ("Aligned endpoint: 1 × 4 × (31 − 1) = 121 frames"), so the caption contradicts the figure and states a false arithmetic equality.
evidence: Rendered page 164 caption: "The fetched implementation uses T_j = (F−1)/4 + 1, H_j = H/16 and W_j = W/16. For aligned F = 4k+1, F = 1+4(T_j−1) = 31 latent time positions correspond to 121 frames." Figure box: "VAE stride (T, H, W) = (4, 16, 16) / Aligned endpoint: 1 × 4 × (31 − 1) = 121 frames". Check: T_j = (121−1)/4 + 1 = 31 ✓; F = 1 + 4(31−1) = 121 ✓; the caption's "= 31" is wrong.
acceptance_test: Rewrite as: "For aligned F = 4k+1, T_j = (F−1)/4 + 1 = 31 latent time positions and F = 1 + 4(T_j−1) = 121 frames." Confirm the caption's two identities match the figure's "Aligned endpoint" box and that no symbol is used for two different quantities.
